messages:
ash: anyone else seeing strange numbers in the org-usage dashboard? looks like Acme's quota burn showing up under unrelated customer rows after the metrics-agg rollout. :alarm_clock:
frances: ugh. which rollout? metrics-aggregate-v3 hit prod earlier today as a 20% canary. I added a grouping optimization to reduce cardinality.
sam: can you repro + paste a minimal query/response?
ash: repro steps: open Admin -> Org Usage -> set time window last 1h -> table shows org 555 with 12k tokens, but request header X-Org-ID=888 (my org). Clicking into row reveals payload with ownerOrg=555 in the body.
ash: trace snippet:
```
POST /internal/metrics/aggregate HTTP/1.1
Host: metricspipeline.internal
X-Org-ID: 888
X-Request-ID: r-abc123
Body: {"group_by": ["service","metric_name"], "filters": {"org":888}}
Response: {"rows": [{"service":"inference","metric_name":"tokens","value":12000,"org":555}], "cached": true}
```
frances: interesting — pipeline response includes org 555 even though request asked for 888. that suggests the aggregator key is deduping by service+metric_name only, and the cached aggregated blob is being reused across orgs. my optimization removed org from the cache key to reduce unique keys.
kai: was that change behind a feature flag or part of the canary?
frances: it was part of metrics-aggregate-v3 canary. i intended to rely on per-org filters at query time, but the aggregation was computed global and then sliced, which explains the mismatch.
bella: immediate actions: 1) disable canary 2) invalidate aggregator cache 3) notify affected customers 4) add runtime guard to detect org mismatch. any objections?
sam: disagree about immediate full invalidation if it's huge; prefer guard first (bypass cache on org mismatch) then targeted purge for keys created since rollout start.
ash: also add a quick paging alert: if any API returns cached=true and response.org not equal request.org, page oncall.
frances: will open PR to restore org into cache-key: `agg:{org}:{service}:{metric_hash}` and add a safety assertion that cached row.org == request.org. adding unit + integration tests.
ash: can we also add a canary UX change: a rollout toggle that shows an explicit "isolate-by-tenant" checkbox so these optimizations can't accidentally drop tenant dimension? rollout UX would default it on for any aggregation changes.
aiops-bot: incident draft created: INC-2026 - metrics-agg cross-tenant exposure.
ops-csm: flagged customers: acme-inc (reported), 2 more possible. notified CSMs.
sam: rolling metrics-aggregate-v3 canary down to 0% now.
deploy-bot: deploy request received: rollback metrics-aggregate-v3 -> executing
deploy-bot: rollback complete 44D
frances: opening PR with revert + key fix. also adding a runtime assertion that if a cached response contains an `org` field not matching the X-Org-ID header, we log at warn and return a 409/clear cache path.
bella: runbook updates: add a checklist for any cache-key or aggregation change: 1) add tenant token to key template 2) e2e verify response.org for sample orgs 3) set canary to 1% with 24h observation before bumping.
aiops-bot: telemetry alert rule created: metrics.prefetch.org_mismatch -> page threshold=1
ash: follow-up: schedule postmortem and include a small spike to run a scan across cache namespace to list keys lacking `{org}` token. runbook item for ops to purge those keys pre-rolling.
frances: noted — will coordinate with infra to run a scheduled scan and present results in the postmortem. tagging @security for exposure review.
ops-csm: CSMs told customers and offered data scrub if they want.
ash: one more suggestion: add a lint in our infra-libs that rejects cache-key templates missing `{org}` or `{tenant_id}` for any service that returns tenant-scoped payloads.
ash: ok will file infra-libs issue.
sam: capturing action items: rollback complete, cache-scan scheduled, PR incoming, alert active, postmortem scheduled. I'll own the follow-up ticket.
